Adventure environment-card role, orders and creature-location rumors (PE 53.16)
===============================================================================

Scope and image ownership
-------------------------
The screenshot's location rumors belong to Steam legacy adventure renderer
0x14080d5e0..0x1408189ac and classic 0x14080ae60..0x14081622c. The relevant
natural-environment card source is extracted at 0x80dbba..0x810a88, classic
0x80b43a..0x80e308. This is distinct from fortress/world site news formatter
0x1da280 (classic 0x1da210), whose paragraphs begin "In {date},".

image-sources.json identifies the configured original PE files and complete
procedure spans. The .asm files preserve original instructions and annotate
literal operands; native-branches.tsv contains conditional branches and
native-switches.tsv decodes all 51 biome and 11 site-name-row selections.
These files are original source evidence, not simulated display or tests.

Card structure and complete production relationship
--------------------------------------------------
The border is drawn at 0x80dc00..0x80dcc5, using original glyph values through
0x80dcaf -> 0xadaad0. The position is derived from dimensions/current pointer,
and is not a fixed screenshot rectangle. Title row 1 uses the containing
region's English name (a946e0) at 0x80dd5d -> 0x80de10; row 2 uses the second
region name at 0x80de64 -> 0x80de7f. Biome classification f569d0 selects all
0..50 native types via the 818614 table; >50 prints no biome text.

Temperature (label 80eabf), Trees (80ecf2), Other Vegetation (80eee7), and
Surroundings (80f08a) are four separate caption/value rows. Their complete
literal families are in native-literals.tsv. Site-name rows begin at y=10:
each visible site gives its original-language name (a94030), its English
name in quotes (a946e0), and a type description assembled from 10cbe10,
aa3770 and 10cbe50. The 0..10 site selector table is 8186e0; unknown types
produce no site-name rows. If there is no site, a separate native construction
row can appear, including "Multiple Constructions". River labels select
Major River/River/Minor River/Stream/Brook. Mountain and Volcano headings are
independent. The native prose production below follows these location rows.

This natural-environment path has no civilization/population footer and needs
none for identifying its frame. W/E compass characters appear in different
later portions of the same owner (81678a..816896), not this ecology/status
path. N/S/E/W and diagonal bearings at 815f4c..816396 belong to strongest-odor
and local-map directions. Existing adventure-smell owner extraction preserves
those separate paths; they are not inputs to this rumor grammar.

Prose container 0x1418a8bb0 (classic 0x1418a2b80) is cached by world-map
coordinate values at 0x1418a8ba8/bac (classic 0x1418a2b78/7c). On coordinate
change, e37d0 clears it, then roles, drive orders and creature-location
rumors are appended in that order. Reuse skips rebuilding and directly
renders its retained native fragments. The append function d51eb0 parses
[C:...] color changes and [B] paragraph breaks. d51c80 applies current native
width to retained text. 810945..810a88 draws each rich fragment using its
stored color (+0x20/+0x21/+0x22), position (+0x28/+0x2c), and ad9960. Text can
be split on spaces into multiple draw calls; the main sentence and optional
suffix can span rows, colors and fragments.

Shared guards and location predicate
------------------------------------
Both task/role and beast blocks require native mode global == 1 and current
adventurer index != -1. The local list at rbp+0xf0 contains eligible visible
site IDs. Native e1420 looks up a candidate site in that list; a result -1
suppresses its paragraph. These decisions change visibility, not wording.

Task/role source resolution walks the current adventurer HF's general links
(virtual kind 0xd), resolves its army-related record via 75500, then uses
record+0x1c4 as entity ID and record+0x1c8 as position ID. The entity's
positions.own vector is +0x10c0; 1ba140 selects position.id at +0x20. The
role text is read directly from selected position+0x218. This is squad[0]:
df.entity.xml defines six preceding two-string arrays at +0x98 (name), +0xd8
(name_female), +0x118 (name_male), +0x158 (spouse), +0x198 (spouse_female),
+0x1d8 (spouse_male), then +0x218 (squad). The pre-existing variant-3 comment
in native_history_positions.inc calls this a spouse field, but the actual
structure and RAW [SQUAD] production identify it as a squad-member title.
Native code does not select a generic/female/male fallback if this field is
empty. Site
membership 9364d0 must resolve and its +0x1c bit 0 must be set.

1. Role paragraph
-----------------
For every eligible site membership, emit exactly:
  [C:3:0:1]You are a {position+0x218} based in {site}.[B]

Main literal 80fefe; dynamic role append 80ff1f; site b93930 at 80ff4b with
r9=0; submit d51eb0 at 80ff71. There are no optional role sentence suffixes.
Current vanilla RAW [SQUAD] singular labels are soldier, militia-dwarf,
fortress guard and ranger. raw-role-sources.tsv retains every source line,
entity, position and plural. Mod-added values are open-ended. These are member
type labels, not player-customized squad.alias values. The role field and
generated site name include their real empty-field cases; they are not finite
English sentence alternatives.

2. Drive-order paragraphs
-------------------------
Walk the resolved army-record task vector +0xb8. Keep tasks whose +0xc HF ID
matches the current adventurer HF. Its virtual +0x18 type is either 8 or 5;
every other task type adds no drive paragraph. Each task must target a site
in the visible local site list.

Both task types emit:
  [C:2:0:1]You have been ordered to drive {entity} from {site}.
  [optional]  You should report the task as complete.
  [B]

Type 8 main begins at 810069 and type 5 at 810418. In both, task+0x20 is
the entity ID, supplied by b92900(r9=0), and task+0x24 is the site ID, supplied
by b93930(r9=0). Missing entity/site can use their native unknown fallbacks.
Type 8 completion literal is 8103a1; type 5 completion literal is 8105b2.
Rich submit calls are 8103d5 and 8105e6. No other drive suffix exists.

Type 8's completion branch: resolve entity and site; scan entity+0x1408
population components within the site's x/y bounding rectangle, sum population
vectors, and treat a qualifying component as still present unless its special
type-1 flag makes it ignorable. Then walk active local units that are not
excluded by +0x110 bit 1, have entity affiliation +0x1208, match task entity,
and belong to the resolved site (13a5660). If neither qualifying population
nor active unit remains, or required entity/site is missing, append completed.

Type 5's completion branch: resolve entity/site and site's governing entity
(9b4e70). Depending on the target entity type: type1 compares that governing
entity directly; types7/4 use 6af0d0 relationship predicate; type0 scans
its links +0xb8 for virtual kind1 matching the governing entity ID. If the
presence/relationship predicate fails, or any required lookup fails, append
completed. Both branches preserve the order main -> completion -> paragraph.

3. Creature-location rumor paragraph
------------------------------------
Loop global rumor vector 0x142643d78 (classic 0x14263dc68). A record has HF ID
+0x00, site ID +0x04, and flags +0x28. A site outside the visible local list
suppresses the whole record. Every accepted record emits:
  [C:4:0:1]{capitalized historical_figure_name} is rumored to be in {site}.

At 8106ec, 72080 initializes the HF context: flags=0, context pointers=0,
current/replacement HF IDs=-1. At 810713, b92f10 is called with fifth=0 and
sixth=0. 52d650 then capitalizes the complete identity before appending it.
At 81075f, b93930 supplies site ID+0x04 with r9=0 (English name, no LPAGE).

The following independent guards append suffixes in this exact order:
  record+0x28 & 2:
    "  [C:7:0:0]This is common knowledge where you are from."
    literal 81077d.
  current adventurer HF resolves and 6943a0(adventurer, rumor HF) returns true:
    "  [C:5:0:1]This creature is known to be dead."
    literal 8107bd. The complete known-death function (all chained unwind
    ranges through 694902) is preserved; it resolves contextual knowledge,
    not just the target HF's death field.
  each matching task in army-record+0xb8: task HF+0xc matches the current
  adventurer, virtual kind=7 and task target HF+0x20 matches record HF:
    "  [C:2:0:1]You have been ordered to kill this creature."
    literal 810863.
    If that target HF resolves and its death field +0x30 != -1, append:
      "  You should report the task as complete."
      literal 810890. This completion suffix depends on the matching kill
      task; it does not depend on whether the known-dead suffix was emitted.
    Multiple matching tasks can repeat the kill/completion pair.
  Finally append [B] (8108d4) and submit the rich paragraph (8108f5).

No report-completed-only beast suffix, alternate rumor opening, finite monster
race switch or dated-news formatter is present in this producer. Dynamic
monster kinds, names, curse display strings and site names come from the
suppliers below. All instruction RVAs in these three producers map to classic
by subtracting 0x2780. Helper offsets have their own explicit original spans.

4. Historical-figure identity for this actual caller
---------------------------------------------------
The full b92f10 procedure is preserved. Several its generic-context branches
are unreachable for this caller's freshly initialized default context: replacing
interrogator/subject, hidden identities, I/me/my/myself, LPAGE tags, possessive
name forms and same-caste comparisons to supplied current/replacement figures.
They remain in original source but must not be invented for this card.

Resolve the rumor HF. A missing HF emits "an unknown creature". Otherwise,
determine whether caste/species should precede its name. It starts true, becomes
false for certain historical-figure flags (+0xc8 entry bits 2/3), is forced
true by curse zombie component +0x160 or visible title byte +0x88, and is
false if the HF race is -1. This caller's sixth argument is 0 and therefore
does not suppress caste automatically.

HF has-name (+0xaa) true:
  caste/species enabled:
    "the " + optional "zombie " + optional "ghostly " + caste_or_race_RAW
    + optional " " + visible curse display-name + " " + complete English name
  caste/species disabled:
    complete English name
HF has-name false:
  "a " + optional "zombie " + optional "ghostly " + singular species_RAW
  + optional " " + visible curse display-name

zombie checks curse+0x160; ghostly checks historical-figure first +0xc8 entry
bit7 and is suppressed when a visible curse display title exists. Caste RAW
singular is preferred if valid and nonempty, then race RAW singular; invalid
or empty RAW fields can contribute no species text. The unnamed branch uses
aa3bd0 for caste/race singular; the named prefix branch reads the equivalent
RAW fields directly. No missing-RAW label is invented. Visible curse+0x90
is a native generated/mod-added display string and can be empty.

Complete English names are supplied by a946e0(hf+0x38, English=true, other=false).
This includes first name, compounded generated surname, and generated epithet
with its native articles/of/possessive components. Screenshot strings such as
Or Glimmeredfigures and Enggo Esteemedfells the Confidence of Hide are dynamic
world names, not fixed literal operands to copy into a glossary.

Site b93930 resolves the ID, calls a946e0(site name, English=true, other=false),
then appends the complete result. Missing site emits "an unknown site". An
existing unnamed site may contribute an empty name. Entity b92900 similarly
supplies native complete English entity names and "an unknown civilization"
when unresolved, despite accepting any historical entity type. Preserve those
source roles so generated-name translation handles
whole names without reinterpreting prose words as names.

Stock curse-generation source material and identity vocabulary already reside
in adventure-threat-rumors/vanilla-curse-fields.tsv and its copied native RAW/
Lua sources. Those are shared dynamic title suppliers; threat-speech sentence
branches are not additional sentences in this environment-card producer.
